# Discussion Board Business Overview and Objectives

## Overview
This document outlines the business vision, operational objectives, and scope of the Discussion Board platform dedicated to the open exchange of ideas and information on political and economic topics. The platform is designed to foster meaningful dialogues, ensuring a safe, respectful, and high-quality environment for all users, regardless of their background or opinion.

## Vision
The Discussion Board aspires to be the leading digital space where diverse perspectives on political and economic issues converge. By providing a structured, moderated, and user-friendly experience, the platform seeks to cultivate a community that values critical thinking, evidence-based debate, and civil discourse. The end goal is to contribute positively to societal understanding and democratic processes through inclusive conversations.

## Business Objectives
- **Enable Informed Discussions:** Provide reliable tools for users to share knowledge, insights, and opinions on trending political and economic matters.
- **Foster Diversity of Thought:** Encourage respectful participation from individuals with a wide range of backgrounds and viewpoints.
- **Ensure Safety and Civility:** Maintain a robust moderation system that addresses abusive behavior, misinformation, and off-topic content while protecting freedom of expression.
- **Drive User Engagement:** Promote active participation through intuitive features—such as voting, commenting, and content sharing—to build a loyal, returning user base.
- **Support Trusted Moderation:** Empower moderators with clear guidelines and efficient tools to manage discussions and upholding the platform’s standards.
- **Continuous Improvement:** Use data-driven insights and feedback loops to refine platform features, moderation policies, and overall user experience.

## Target Audience
- Individuals interested in engaging with political and economic topics
- Professionals, students, and enthusiasts in related fields
- Organizations and communities fostering civil discourse

## Key Features Overview
- Topic-centric discussion threads for both current events and timeless issues
- User authentication and flexible onboarding experiences
- Multi-role system (member, moderator, admin) to enhance operational governance
- Voting, commenting, and content reaction capabilities
- Robust reporting, flagging, and moderation workflows

## Success Metrics
- Growth in user registrations and daily active usage
- High engagement rates (posts, comments, reactions per user)
- Low incidence rates of rule violations and effective moderation response times
- Positive feedback from user satisfaction surveys
- Sustainable retention and expansion of the core user community

## Value Proposition
The Discussion Board delivers a one-stop platform for high-quality conversations on pressing political and economic issues, safeguarding civil exchange and drawing on collective intelligence. By balancing ease of use with principled moderation, the service meets the needs of both casual participants and expert contributors, ensuring every voice can contribute to the evolving public discourse.

# Discussion Board User Roles and Access Control

## 1. Introduction
This document outlines the user roles, permission sets, authentication workflows, and access control logic for the Discussion Board service. Properly delineating these controls ensures a safe, fair, and manageable community space for the exchange of political and economic opinions.

---

## 2. User Roles Overview

| Role        | Description                                                                 |
|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Member      | General users who can post, comment on, and react to board content.         |
| Moderator   | Users who monitor content, handle reports, and enforce community standards. |
| Admin       | System operators who manage all configurations, policies, and users.        |

<!-- See [03_DiscussionBoard_Main_Features_and_User_Journeys.md](./03_DiscussionBoard_Main_Features_and_User_Journeys.md) for detailed flows by role. -->

---

## 3. Permissions Matrix

| Action                                | Member | Moderator | Admin |
|----------------------------------------|:------:|:---------:|:-----:|
| Register & Authenticate                |   ✓    |     ✓     |  ✓   |
| View Posts & Comments                  |   ✓    |     ✓     |  ✓   |
| Create Post/Comment                    |   ✓    |     ✓     |  ✓   |
| Edit Own Post/Comment                  |   ✓    |     ✓     |  ✓   |
| Delete Own Post/Comment                |   ✓    |     ✓     |  ✓   |
| React (Like/Dislike) to Posts/Comments |   ✓    |     ✓     |  ✓   |
| Report Posts/Comments                  |   ✓    |     ✓     |  ✓   |
| Moderate (Edit/Delete Any Post/Comment)|        |     ✓     |  ✓   |
| Resolve Reports                        |        |     ✓     |  ✓   |
| Manage User Roles/Access               |        |           |  ✓   |
| Configure Board Settings/Policy        |        |           |  ✓   |

---

## 4. Access Control & Authentication

- **Registration**: New users register via email or social login; basic verification required.
- **Authentication**: Secure login using username/password or supported OAuth providers.
- **Session Management**: JWT or session cookie used to maintain identity and ensure role-based access enforcement.
- **Role Assignment**: Default role is Member upon registration. Elevated roles (Moderator, Admin) require Admin intervention.
- **Access Validation**: Every sensitive API endpoint enforces authentication and checks role-based permissions per the matrix.

---

## 5. Role Elevation & Demotion Processes
- **Promotion to Moderator/Admin**: Only Admins can elevate users. Such actions must be audited and ideally require secondary authorization, especially for Admin role changes.
- **Demotion/Revocation**: Admin removes elevated rights as needed, based on performance or conduct, with audit trails for accountability.

---

## 6. Security & Compliance Considerations
- Enforce password and session security best practices.
- Rate limit login and critical actions to prevent abuse.
- Log all role changes, moderator actions, and admin activities for traceability.
- Ensure privacy compliance (e.g., GDPR) for user data, especially for role or access logs.

See [05_DiscussionBoard_Service_Overview_and_Architecture.md](./05_DiscussionBoard_Service_Overview_and_Architecture.md) for integrated technical overview.

# Main Features & User Journeys of Discussion Board

This document describes the key features and main user journeys of the Discussion Board, covering member, moderator, and admin roles. It provides an overview of core functionality and integrates essential reference summaries to ensure the page is fully self-contained.

## Table of Contents
1. Overview and Objectives
2. Roles and Access Control
3. Main Features
4. User Journeys
5. Business Rules & Moderation
6. Architecture Overview

---

## 1. Overview and Objectives
The Discussion Board is a digital forum designed to foster transparent and civil dialogue on political and economic topics. Its primary objectives are:
- Enable open discussion, knowledge-sharing, and constructive debate among authenticated users.
- Maintain a secure, moderated environment free from abusive content.
- Ensure role-based access to sensitive features and administrative controls.

## 2. Roles and Access Control
Three principal user roles define access and permissions:
- **Member**: Can create posts, comment, and participate in voting (like/dislike).
- **Moderator**: Monitors discussions, resolves disputes, manages reported content, and can edit or remove posts/comments.
- **Admin**: Configures system settings, manages users and roles, sets discussion policies, and oversees high-level moderation procedures.

## 3. Main Features
- Topic boards for political and economic discussions
- Post creation, editing, reporting, and deletion
- Nested commenting with threading support
- Like/Dislike voting on posts and comments
- Reporting mechanism for inappropriate content
- Moderation tools (approve, hide, edit, delete, manage reports)
- Role-based dashboards (tailored for members, moderators, admins)
- Notification system for mentions, replies, and moderation actions
- Search and filter by topic, user, or date

## 4. User Journeys
### Member
- Discover a topic board, create a post, or respond to an existing post
- Participate in comment threads, like/dislike contributions, and report inappropriate content
- Receive feedback via notifications on activity involving them

### Moderator
- Receive alerts for new reports
- Audit flagged posts/comments, using moderation tools to act (warn, edit, remove, escalate)
- Maintain civil discussion per community guidelines

### Admin
- Set up new boards, configure categories, and adjust discussion policies
- Assign moderator privileges and control user registrations
- Review overall system health and handle escalated moderation cases

## 5. Business Rules & Moderation
- Content violating community guidelines (spam, hate speech, etc.) is subject to removal and user sanctioning
- Member actions are logged for accountability
- Moderators must act transparently and cannot moderate their own content
- Automated checks for abuse or coordinated harmful activity support moderator workflows

## 6. Architecture Overview
The system is designed for security, scalability, and easy maintenance. Core components include:
- **User Management**: Authentication, authorization, and role control
- **Content Engine**: Handles creation, retrieval, and moderation of posts/comments
- **Reporting & Moderation Module**: Facilitates workflow for handling inappropriate content
- **Notification Service**: Powers real-time and asynchronous user alerts
- **Search & Indexing**: Enables content discovery through search and filters

---

# Discussion Board Business Rules & Moderation

## Overview
The Discussion Board aims to provide a vibrant, respectful space for exchanging ideas on political and economic topics. Strict business rules and robust moderation policies are essential to foster open, civil, and meaningful discussions. This document describes the rules, content policies, moderation roles, escalation processes, dispute resolution, and reporting mechanisms. It ensures transparent expectations for all users and supports platform success through user trust and community health.

## 1. Participation Rules
- Only registered and authenticated users may participate.
- Users must adhere to all terms of service and community guidelines.
- Posts and comments should stay on-topic (political or economic subjects) and contribute constructively to ongoing discussions.
- Harassment, hate speech, discrimination, or personal attacks are strictly forbidden.
- Spam, off-topic advertising, and solicitation are not permitted.
- Users must respect privacy and never post personal information.

## 2. Content Submission Policies
- Members may create, edit, or delete their own posts and comments.
- All content must remain factual, source-referenced where possible, and free from copyright infringement.
- The use of inappropriate language or graphic content is prohibited.
- Duplicated content and misleading titles are subject to removal.
- Users are responsible for all content published under their account.

## 3. Moderation Workflow
- Moderators and administrators have the authority to monitor all user-generated content.
- Flagged or reported posts and comments are reviewed within 24 hours.
- Moderators may edit, hide, or remove content that violates rules, providing clear reasons for their actions.
- Repeat or severe offenses can lead to temporary or permanent suspensions.
- All disciplinary actions are logged for accountability.

## 4. Reporting Mechanisms
- Any user can report posts or comments suspected of violating the rules.
- Reports are submitted via a designated form and logged with timestamps.
- Users may provide evidence or reasoning within the report.
- Moderators notify reporters of the outcome after review.

## 5. Escalation and Dispute Resolution
- Users can appeal moderation decisions through a formal appeals process.
- Appeals are reviewed by a panel of moderators and at least one administrator.
- Decisions on appeals are communicated in writing within five business days.
- Unresolved disputes may be escalated to the highest platform authority for a final decision.

## 6. Role-Specific Responsibilities
### Member
- Create, comment on, and engage with posts.
- Report inappropriate content.
- Follow platform rules at all times.

### Moderator
- Monitor content and enforce rules in all public contexts.
- Manage reported posts, execute disciplinary actions, and document outcomes.
- Engage with users to clarify policies and resolve minor conflicts.

### Admin
- Oversee moderation processes and make final decisions on escalations.
- Maintain community guidelines, set new policies, and manage high-level user privileges.
- Provide ongoing training for moderators to maintain consistent standards.

## 7. Rule Revision and Transparency
- All business rules and moderation policies are subject to regular review.
- Changes are communicated in advance, with rationale and opportunities for community feedback.
- Policy updates are documented for transparency.

## 8. Acceptance Criteria
- Users receive prompt feedback and rationale for moderation actions.
- Reports are handled efficiently and impartially.
- The moderation system supports a positive, open, and safe discussion environment.
- All roles understand and execute their responsibilities clearly.

## 9. Compliance & Monitoring
- Periodic audits ensure moderator compliance with policies.
- Metrics such as report resolution time and user satisfaction are tracked to guide improvements.
- Repeated failure to comply with rules at any level may lead to retraining or loss of privileges.

The above policies ensure a sustainable, trusted platform for all users while allowing for robust, meaningful debate within a supportive framework.

# 05_DiscussionBoard_Service_Overview_and_Architecture

## 1. Overview
This document outlines the high-level service architecture and core workflows for the Discussion Board, supporting political and economic topic discussions. The architecture is designed to deliver a scalable, user-centric platform that ensures engaging, civil discourse with clearly defined roles such as member, moderator, and admin. This overview avoids technical implementation details, instead focusing on business processes, role interactions, and key integration points.

## 2. Service Architecture
### 2.1 Component Map
- **User Portal:** Unified entry point providing responsive access for all user roles.
- **Authentication & Access Control:** Manages login, registration, and user role validation (member, moderator, admin), ensuring appropriate access levels per user.
- **Discussion Engine:** Core component handling post creation, comments, threads, reactions (like/dislike), and real-time updates.
- **Moderation Hub:** Interface and backend logic for moderator and admin actions — content review, reporting, user management, and dispute resolution.
- **Notification Service:** Provides system alerts for replies, mentions, moderation actions, and announcements.
- **Analytics & Reporting:** Aggregates usage metrics, sentiment trends, and moderation statistics for admins.

### 2.2 Role-Based Interaction Flow
Each role's interaction is governed by robust access policies. 
- **Members:** Create/view posts, comment, react, and engage with reporting.
- **Moderators:** Review and moderate content, manage flagged items, resolve conflicts.
- **Admins:** Configure system-level settings, manage users/roles, oversee policy compliance.

## 3. Workflow Summary
```
flowchart TD
    Login[User Login/Register] --> Home[Main Board View]
    Home -->|Create Post| NewPost[Post Creation]
    Home -->|Read Posts| PostDetail[Post Detail & Comments]
    PostDetail -->|Comment| CommentFlow[Comment Submission]
    PostDetail -->|React| ReactionFlow[Like/Dislike]
    PostDetail -->|Report| ReportFlow[Content Reporting]
    ReportFlow --> ModReview[Moderator Review]
    ModReview -->|Escalate| AdminReview[Admin Action]
    Home -->|Notifications| Notify[Check Alerts]
    AdminReview --> Decision[Resolution/Action]
```

## 4. Integration Points
- **Authentication Service:** Ensures secure, role-based access throughout all interactions.
- **Notification Module:** Integrates with user actions and moderation to keep all participants informed in real-time.
- **Moderation/Reporting:** Tight coupling between user reports, moderator actions, and system analytics for transparency.
- **Analytics export:** Aggregates data for business review and optimization.

## 5. Non-Functional Considerations
- **Scalability:** Designed to support active, large-scale discussions with responsive performance across devices.
- **Security & Privacy:** Implements strict access controls, content moderation, and user privacy safeguards.
- **Auditability:** All critical actions (moderation, admin changes, policy edits) are logged for compliance review.

## 6. High-Level Architectural Diagram
```
flowchart LR
    User[User Portal]
    Auth[Auth & Access Control]
    Discussion[Discussion Engine]
    ModHub[Moderation Hub]
    Notify[Notification Service]
    Analytics[Analytics & Reporting]

    User --> Auth
    Auth --> Discussion
    Discussion --> Notify
    Discussion --> ModHub
    ModHub --> Analytics
    Auth --> Admin[Admin Tools]
    Admin --> Analytics
```

---

For details regarding user role definitions, workflows, and business policies, refer to the corresponding documents in this series.
